what: How much STRUCTURE a car window carries, in units of the one-byte quantisation step at that pane's own level, after removing a fitted smooth quadratic. The floor is anchored by measuring a surface in the SAME frame that is definitionally featureless.
why: Level and content are different questions and this project spent several rounds conflating them. A pane can be lifted well off black and still be a flat sheet. p95/p50 cannot tell a smooth Fresnel ramp from a reflected shopfront; this can.
units: q = one 8-bit code at the pane's own level. An 8-bit-encoded pure ramp already reads Laplacian p99 1.38 q, so zero is not the floor and the floor must be measured, not assumed.

render.surface: smooth bonnet paint, same frame - THE FLOOR

verdict: Every render pane sits at the level of smooth painted sheet metal in its own frame. Real car glass clears that floor by 4-10x. Remove the quadratic and contrast-stretch what is left: the real cars show headrests, parcel shelves, heated-rear-screen elements and door frames; the render panes show ordered dither. The shipped gain moved the LEVEL 3.7x and left this statistic where it was - 0.41 -> 0.73 on the windscreen against a real-glass range of 2.7-4.0, and the WRONG WAY on the backlight, 1.61 -> 1.32.
target: To call a render pane glass: residual above ~2 q and Laplacian p99 above ~8 in this frame, with recognisable shapes in the residual image. That needs CONTENT in the environment. scene.environment is pmrem.fromEquirectangular(this.lut.texture) - the sky LUT alone, no buildings, no street, no cars - so no gain on it can deliver this. The remaining lever is a reflection probe, which is a different order of cost: a per-car cube probe across 30 parked cars and a 30-car fleet.
exception: The 14.7 m car's rear screen carries one genuine specular glow at its lower-left corner, present in BOTH arms and unchanged by this round. It is real content in glass and the gain dilutes it: that pane's p95/p05 falls 1.87 -> 1.42 because an unchanged highlight is now a smaller fraction of a brighter pane.
